central_method: Crespin 2024 fully patient-level-controlled Medicare coding-intensity share (2.0% of MS-DRG payment weights, Exhibit 4; CI 1.7-2.2%) applied to our computed DY2024 FFS IPPS Medicare pool NET of non-scaling outlier+capital add-ons (operating-base pool), recoverability 0.55, less the tiny annualized DOJ FCA-confirmed hospital-upcoding overlap. FLOOR = Crespin CI-low (1.7%) at recoverability 0.45. HIGH = our HCC-risk-net residual on the (plain Fisher) migration (a cruder single-proxy control that over-attributes to coding) at recoverability 0.75. CORRECTED 2026-06-10: the prior build misread Crespin's national $4.6B Medicare figure as five-state and double-scaled it by a 0.176 population share, manufacturing a 21.8% pool share (~11x Crespin's actual 2.0%); that error is fixed.
vs_target: computed central $1.04B is below the $20B scoping target; reported as-is, not tuned (Issue #16/#17 precedent). The gap to target is the data-partner CTA: a national patient-level replication of Crespin could push the controlled share above 2.0% and the recoverable figure toward the risk-net ceiling.
data_partner_cta: Full Crespin five-state regression replication on HCUP NIS/SID microdata (patient-level controls for demographics, LOS, principal diagnosis, hospital characteristics) requires a DUA workflow not run here. CMS LDS/VRDC claim-level files would allow per-discharge coding-intensity audit. These are the explicit recruitment asks for closing the gap from the controlled 2.0% central toward the risk-net ceiling.

ma_selection_test.verdict: After the Crespin correction (Stage 5.5 C1), the CENTRAL is anchored to Crespin's fully patient-level-controlled Medicare coding-intensity share (2.0% of MS-DRG weights; regression on demographics, length-of-stay, Elixhauser comorbidity, hospital fixed effects). Those controls already net out genuine acuity AND compositional selection at the patient level, so the central is selection-robust by Crespin's design, not by ours. Our own risk-net residual (Fisher migration net of the HCC risk-score rise) is a CRUDER single-proxy control and OVER-attributes to coding, so it defines the HIGH/ceiling, not the floor. Selection mechanics still hold: any selection making remaining FFS patients sicker raises the FFS average HCC risk score, which the risk-net method divides out; even if 100% of the FFS risk rise were selection it is netted. And measured FFS acuity FELL 2019->2024 (HCC recalibration + COVID mortality), so post-2019 selection did not inflate measured FFS acuity over the calibration-transfer window. The corrected central is ~$1.0B; the risk-net ceiling is ~$5B.
